explanations.answer: See the land given to Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD tells Moses to "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The land is already given, and Moses gets the view. I bet that climb had him huffing, but what a front-row seat.

explanations.answer: Build an altar to the LORD
explanations.explanation: I get why an altar comes to mind, since mountains and altars go together in a lot of stories. But this time the LORD sends Moses up for a different reason. He says, "…see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) No bricks, no stones, just a long look.

Nobody is mentioned waiting up there with Moses, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The elders aren't in this verse. The LORD gives Moses one job, which is to see the land.

Ooh, I know why this one sounds right. A leader goes all that way with his people, so you'd expect him to walk in with them. But God doesn't say that. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Moses sees the land, and God says he will be gathered to his people.

Right, and it's a tender one. God doesn't say Moses will lead Israel into the land. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Moses gets to see it, and he is gathered to his people.

Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The next verse says why, and it names both brothers, because both of them rebelled against God's command at the waters. So the brothers' stories line up right to the end.
Korah is a fair guess, but it's not the name God gives here. He says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The verse names Aaron, and it calls him Moses' brother.
Caleb is a good name to know, but it's not the one in this verse. God says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Look for the word "brother" and you land on Aaron.

Yes, and God says it straight. He tells Moses, "…both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) Both of them, Moses and Aaron. The text doesn't soften it, so I won't either.

This one is True, and it's a hard one to hear. God says, "…both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) The "…both of you…" means Moses and Aaron. God says it plainly, so we take it plainly.

explanations.answer: A man to lead the congregation
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. Moses has just heard he'll be gathered to his people, and he doesn't start with himself. He asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation" (Numbers 27:16) I think that's a man thinking about the people he's leaving behind. Even with that news, his mind is on them.

I bet plenty of us would ask for that one, me first. But Moses doesn't. He asks, "May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation" (Numbers 27:16) His request is about who leads next, not about himself.

explanations.answer: A way into the land after all
explanations.explanation: Good guess, because that's what a lot of us would beg for. But the text doesn't have Moses asking that. He asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation" (Numbers 27:16) His request is for the people's next leader.

Yes, sheep. Moses asks for a leader so that "…the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep with no shepherd are like a batch of cookies with nobody watching the timer. Nobody is looking out for them, and that's how things end up burnt. Jesus uses this same picture when He sees the crowds and has compassion on them. (Matthew 9:36)

Soldiers is a fair guess, but Moses picks a different picture. He says the congregation of the LORD "…will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) I think a shepherd is a much gentler picture than a commander.

Travelers is a fair guess, but Moses doesn't reach for a map. He says, "…so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep can't read a map, friend. Earlier in that same verse, Moses asks for a man who will "…go out and come in before them…" and that's what a shepherd does.
Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) Look at what God points to. He doesn't read out a résumé. He names who is in the man.
Strength is a natural guess, but it's not the word God uses. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) The thing God points to is the Spirit.
Fire sounds mighty dramatic, I'll admit. But God doesn't call Joshua a man with fire in him. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) Save the fire for my ovens.
That's the one. God says, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) It's a simple act, and Moses does it when the time comes (Numbers 27:23).
Oil does show up elsewhere in Scripture, so it's a smart guess. But God doesn't mention oil here. He says, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) Hands, nothing poured.
A staff handoff would make a great picture, wouldn't it? But the text doesn't say that here. God's instruction is, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) No staff in this instruction.

This one is False, friend. God wants it out in the open. He says, "Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) Nothing private about it.

Right, False. God wants it out in the open. Joshua is to "…stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation…" and be commissioned "…in their sight…" (Numbers 27:19) That's the opposite of private.

explanations.answer: So the congregation will obey him
explanations.explanation: That's the reason, friend. God says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) Notice it says some of Moses' authority, and the point is that the people will follow him. A new leader with nothing behind him gets a lot of shrugs, and this one gets backing in front of everybody.

explanations.answer: So Moses can rest on the mountain
explanations.explanation: The text never says that. God gives a different reason: "…so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) It's about the people following Joshua. Moses taking a nap doesn't come into it.

explanations.answer: So Joshua can judge every case
explanations.explanation: I see why it sounds right, since leaders handle a lot of cases. But the text doesn't give that reason. God says, "…so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) The goal is that the people obey.
Counsel, you got it. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Eleazar does the seeking, and he does it for Joshua before the LORD.

Mercy is a lovely word, but it's not the one God uses here. He says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Counsel is guidance for the road ahead.

Blessing is a nice thought, but it's not the word in this verse. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) It's counsel, the kind you ask for when a decision is coming.

True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. Now THAT is how you follow a recipe, baker. No skipped steps.

This one is True. After God finishes speaking, the text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
